rows: Engineers who like translating a technical constraint into a decision a business can act on.
Almost nobody enters PM straight after B.Tech with zero experience. Most product managers spent 2-4 years first as an engineer, analyst, or in a related function.
Engineers who understand the technical side but want to sit closer to business decisions.
Only pays off with a genuine business interest and a strong program or work-experience base first, not as an escape from a branch you dislike.

items.heading: Confirm Branch Eligibility
items.text: Confirm branch eligibility. UPSC ESE currently recruits through Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, and Electronics & Telecommunications engineering. If your branch is not one of these four, this specific exam is not your route; look at step-PSU or UPSC CSE instead.

items.heading: Clear the Preliminary Stage
items.text: Clear the Preliminary stage. Objective papers on General Studies and Engineering Aptitude, plus a branch-specific paper. This stage filters out the vast majority of the roughly 2-3 lakh applicants.

items.heading: Clear the Mains
items.text: Clear the Mains. Conventional, written-answer papers in your specific engineering discipline. This is where genuine subject depth from your B.Tech years actually matters again.

items.heading: Personality Test and Allocation
items.text: Personality Test and allocation. Final interview, then allocation to services like the Indian Railways Service of Electrical Engineers, Central Public Works Department, or Indian Defence Service of Engineers, based on rank and preference.

items.text: Non-software roles do not pay as well, so take whatever software offer you get, even a weak one.

items.text: Core-branch jobs are dying, so branch does not matter anymore.
